title: Episode 4: The Weight of the Bharata

ending.reason: §2 ¶8 ends the full list of the hundred parvas ("...the very wonderful Bhavishyaparva"); ¶9 is a bridge ("as follows:") into the eighteen-parva summary, which begins a new long catalogue.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The study of the Bharata is an act of piety.
lines.tts_text: The study of the Bharata is an act of piety.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: He that readeth even one foot, with belief, hath his sins entirely purged away.
lines.tts_text: He that readeth even one foot, with belief, hath his sins entirely purged away.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Herein Devas, Devarshis, and immaculate Brahmarshis of good deeds, have been spoken of; and likewise Yakshas and great Uragas (Nagas).
lines.tts_text: Herein Devas, Devarshis, and immaculate Brahmarshis of good deeds, have been spoken of; and likewise Yakshas and great Uragas.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Herein also hath been described the eternal Vasudeva possessing the six attributes.
lines.tts_text: Herein also hath been described the eternal Vasudeva possessing the six attributes.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: He is the true and just, the pure and holy, the eternal Brahma, the supreme soul, the true constant light, whose divine deeds wise and learned recount; from whom hath proceeded the non-existent and existent-non-existent universe with principles of generation and progression, and birth, death and re-birth.
lines.tts_text: He is the true and just, the pure and holy, the eternal Brahma, the supreme soul, the true constant light, whose divine deeds wise and learned recount; from whom hath proceeded the non-existent and existent-non-existent universe with principles of generation and progression, and birth, death and re-birth.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: That also hath been treated of which is called Adhyatma (the superintending spirit of nature) that partaketh of the attributes of the five elements.
lines.tts_text: That also hath been treated of which is called Adhyatma that partaketh of the attributes of the five elements.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: That also hath been described who is purusha being above such epithets as 'undisplayed' and the like; also that which the foremost yatis exempt from the common destiny and endued with the power of meditation and Tapas behold dwelling in their hearts as a reflected image in the mirror.
lines.tts_text: That also hath been described who is purusha being above such epithets as 'undisplayed' and the like; also that which the foremost yatis exempt from the common destiny and endued with the power of meditation and Tapas behold dwelling in their hearts as a reflected image in the mirror.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The man of faith, devoted to piety, and constant in the exercise of virtue, on reading this section is freed from sin.
lines.tts_text: The man of faith, devoted to piety, and constant in the exercise of virtue, on reading this section is freed from sin.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The believer that constantly heareth recited this section of the Bharata, called the Introduction, from the beginning, falleth not into difficulties.
lines.tts_text: The believer that constantly heareth recited this section of the Bharata, called the Introduction, from the beginning, falleth not into difficulties.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The man repeating any part of the introduction in the two twilights is during such act freed from the sins contracted during the day or the night.
lines.tts_text: The man repeating any part of the introduction in the two twilights is during such act freed from the sins contracted during the day or the night.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: This section, the body of the Bharata, is truth and nectar.
lines.tts_text: This section, the body of the Bharata, is truth and nectar.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: As butter is in curd, Brahmana among bipeds, the Aranyaka among the Vedas, and nectar among medicines; as the sea is eminent among receptacles of water, and the cow among quadrupeds; as are these (among the things mentioned) so is the Bharata said to be among histories.
lines.tts_text: As butter is in curd, Brahmana among bipeds, the Aranyaka among the Vedas, and nectar among medicines; as the sea is eminent among receptacles of water, and the cow among quadrupeds; as are these so is the Bharata said to be among histories.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: He that causeth it, even a single foot thereof, to be recited to Brahmanas during a Sradha, his offerings of food and drink to the manes of his ancestors become inexhaustible.
lines.tts_text: He that causeth it, even a single foot thereof, to be recited to Brahmanas during a Sradha, his offerings of food and drink to the manes of his ancestors become inexhaustible.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: By the aid of history and the Puranas, the Veda may be expounded; but the Veda is afraid of one of little information lest he should it.
lines.tts_text: By the aid of history and the Puranas, the Veda may be expounded; but the Veda is afraid of one of little information lest he should injure it.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The learned man who recites to other this Veda of Vyasa reapeth advantage.
lines.tts_text: The learned man who recites to others this Veda of Vyasa reapeth advantage.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: It may without doubt destroy even the sin of killing the embryo and the like.
lines.tts_text: It may without doubt destroy even the sin of killing the embryo and the like.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: He that readeth this holy chapter of the moon, readeth the whole of the Bharata, I ween.
lines.tts_text: He that readeth this holy chapter of the moon, readeth the whole of the Bharata, I ween.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The man who with reverence daily listeneth to this sacred work acquireth long life and renown and ascendeth to heaven.
lines.tts_text: The man who with reverence daily listeneth to this sacred work acquireth long life and renown and ascendeth to heaven.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: In former days, having placed the four Vedas on one side and the Bharata on the other, these were weighed in the balance by the celestials assembled for that purpose.
lines.tts_text: In former days, having placed the four Vedas on one side and the Bharata on the other, these were weighed in the balance by the celestials assembled for that purpose.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: And as the latter weighed heavier than the four Vedas with their mysteries, from that period it hath been called in the world Mahabharata (the great Bharata).
lines.tts_text: And as the latter weighed heavier than the four Vedas with their mysteries, from that period it hath been called in the world Mahabharata.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Being esteemed superior both in substance and gravity of import it is denominated Mahabharata on account of such substance and gravity of import.
lines.tts_text: Being esteemed superior both in substance and gravity of import it is denominated Mahabharata on account of such substance and gravity of import.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: He that knoweth its meaning is saved from all his sins.
lines.tts_text: He that knoweth its meaning is saved from all his sins.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: 'Tapa is innocent, study is harmless, the ordinance of the Vedas prescribed for all the tribes are harmless, the acquisition of wealth by exertion is harmless; but when they are abused in their practices it is then that they become sources of evil.'
lines.tts_text: 'Tapa is innocent, study is harmless, the ordinance of the Vedas prescribed for all the tribes are harmless, the acquisition of wealth by exertion is harmless; but when they are abused in their practices it is then that they become sources of evil.'

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The Rishis said,
lines.tts_text: The Rishis said,

lines.speaker: naimisha_rishis
lines.text: O son of Suta, we wish to hear a full and circumstantial account of the place mentioned by you as Samanta-panchaya.
lines.tts_text: O son of Suta, we wish to hear a full and circumstantial account of the place mentioned by you as Samantapanchaka.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Sauti said,
lines.tts_text: Sauti said,

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Listen, O ye Brahmanas, to the sacred descriptions I utter O ye best of men, ye deserve to hear of the place known as Samanta-panchaka.
lines.tts_text: Listen, O ye Brahmanas, to the sacred descriptions I utter O ye best of men, ye deserve to hear of the place known as Samantapanchaka.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: In the interval between the Treta and Dwapara Yugas, Rama (the son of Jamadagni) great among all who have borne arms, urged by impatience of wrongs, repeatedly smote the noble race of Kshatriyas.
lines.tts_text: In the interval between the Treta and Dwapara Yugas, Rama great among all who have borne arms, urged by impatience of wrongs, repeatedly smote the noble race of Kshatriyas.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: And when that fiery meteor, by his own valour, annihilated the entire tribe of the Kshatriyas, he formed at Samanta-panchaka five lakes of blood.
lines.tts_text: And when that fiery meteor, by his own valour, annihilated the entire tribe of the Kshatriyas, he formed at Samantapanchaka five lakes of blood.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: We are told that his reason being overpowered by anger he offered oblations of blood to the manes of his ancestors, standing in the midst of the sanguine waters of those lakes.
lines.tts_text: We are told that his reason being overpowered by anger he offered oblations of blood to the manes of his ancestors, standing in the midst of the sanguine waters of those lakes.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: It was then that his forefathers of whom Richika was the first having arrived there addressed him thus, 'O Rama, O blessed Rama, O offspring of Bhrigu, we have been gratified with the reverence thou hast shown for thy ancestors and with thy valour, O mighty one!
lines.tts_text: It was then that his forefathers of whom Richika was the first having arrived there addressed him thus, 'O Rama, O blessed Rama, O offspring of Bhrigu, we have been gratified with the reverence thou hast shown for thy ancestors and with thy valour, O mighty one!
lines.direction: Sauti quoting the ancestors' blessing; grave and warm

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Blessings be upon thee.
lines.tts_text: Blessings be upon thee.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: O thou illustrious one, ask the boon that thou mayst desire.
lines.tts_text: O thou illustrious one, ask the boon that thou mayst desire.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Rama said,
lines.tts_text: Rama said,

lines.speaker: parasurama
lines.text: If, O fathers, ye are favourably disposed towards me, the boon I ask is that I may be absolved from the sins born of my having annihilated the Kshatriyas in anger, and that the lakes I have formed may become famous in the world as holy shrines.
lines.tts_text: If, O fathers, ye are favourably disposed towards me, the boon I ask is that I may be absolved from the sins born of my having annihilated the Kshatriyas in anger, and that the lakes I have formed may become famous in the world as holy shrines.
lines.direction: the warrior-sage, spent after his vengeance, asking to be absolved; grave, remorseful, still mighty

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The Pitris then said,
lines.tts_text: The Pitris then said,

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: So shall it be.
lines.tts_text: So shall it be.
lines.direction: the ancestors' answer, voiced by the narrator (no crowd voice)

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: But be thou pacified.
lines.tts_text: But be thou pacified.
lines.direction: the ancestors' answer, voiced by the narrator (no crowd voice)

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: And Rama was pacified accordingly.
lines.tts_text: And Rama was pacified accordingly.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The region that lieth near unto those lakes of gory water, from that time hath been celebrated as Samanta-panchaka the holy.
lines.tts_text: The region that lieth near unto those lakes of gory water, from that time hath been celebrated as Samantapanchaka the holy.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The wise have declared that every country should be distinguished by a name significant of some circumstance which may have rendered it famous.
lines.tts_text: The wise have declared that every country should be distinguished by a name significant of some circumstance which may have rendered it famous.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: In the interval between the Dwapara and the Kali Yugas there happened at Samanta-panchaka the encounter between the armies of the Kauravas and the Pandavas.
lines.tts_text: In the interval between the Dwapara and the Kali Yugas there happened at Samantapanchaka the encounter between the armies of the Kauravas and the Pandavas.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: In that holy region, without ruggedness of any kind, were assembled eighteen Akshauhinis of soldiers eager for battle.
lines.tts_text: In that holy region, without ruggedness of any kind, were assembled eighteen Akshauhinis of soldiers eager for battle.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: And, O Brahmanas, having come thereto, they were all slain on the spot.
lines.tts_text: And, O Brahmanas, having come thereto, they were all slain on the spot.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Thus the name of that region, O Brahmanas, hath been explained, and the country described to you as a sacred and delightful one.
lines.tts_text: Thus the name of that region, O Brahmanas, hath been explained, and the country described to you as a sacred and delightful one.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: I have mentioned the whole of what relateth to it as the region is celebrated throughout the three worlds.'
lines.tts_text: I have mentioned the whole of what relateth to it as the region is celebrated throughout the three worlds.'

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The Rishis said,
lines.tts_text: The Rishis said,

lines.speaker: naimisha_rishis
lines.text: We have a desire to know, O son of Suta, what is implied by the term Akshauhini that hath been used by thee.
lines.tts_text: We have a desire to know, O son of Suta, what is implied by the term Akshauhini that hath been used by thee.

lines.speaker: naimisha_rishis
lines.text: Tell us in full what is the number of horse and foot, chariots and elephants, which compose an Akshauhini for thou art fully informed.
lines.tts_text: Tell us in full what is the number of horse and foot, chariots and elephants, which compose an Akshauhini for thou art fully informed.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Sauti said,
lines.tts_text: Sauti said,

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: One chariot, one elephant, five foot-soldiers, and three horses form one Patti; three pattis make one Sena-mukha; three sena-mukhas are called a Gulma; three gulmas, a Gana; three ganas, a Vahini; three vahinis together are called a Pritana; three pritanas form a Chamu; three chamus, one Anikini; and an anikini taken ten times forms, as it is styled by those who know, an Akshauhini.
lines.tts_text: One chariot, one elephant, five foot-soldiers, and three horses form one Patti; three pattis make one Sena-mukha; three sena-mukhas are called a Gulma; three gulmas, a Gana; three ganas, a Vahini; three vahinis together are called a Pritanaa; three Pritanaas form a Chamu; three chamus, one Anikini; and an anikini taken ten times forms, as it is styled by those who know, an Akshauhini.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: O ye best of Brahmanas, arithmeticians have calculated that the number of chariots in an Akshauhini is twenty-one thousand eight hundred and seventy.
lines.tts_text: O ye best of Brahmanas, arithmeticians have calculated that the number of chariots in an Akshauhini is twenty-one thousand eight hundred and seventy.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The measure of elephants must be fixed at the same number.
lines.tts_text: The measure of elephants must be fixed at the same number.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: O ye pure, you must know that the number of foot-soldiers is one hundred and nine thousand, three hundred and fifty, the number of horse is sixty-five thousand, six hundred and ten.
lines.tts_text: O ye pure, you must know that the number of foot-soldiers is one hundred and nine thousand, three hundred and fifty, the number of horse is sixty-five thousand, six hundred and ten.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: These, O Brahmanas, as fully explained by me, are the numbers of an Akshauhini as said by those acquainted with the principles of numbers.
lines.tts_text: These, O Brahmanas, as fully explained by me, are the numbers of an Akshauhini as said by those acquainted with the principles of numbers.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: O best of Brahmanas, according to this calculation were composed the eighteen Akshauhinis of the Kaurava and the Pandava army.
lines.tts_text: O best of Brahmanas, according to this calculation were composed the eighteen Akshauhinis of the Kaurava and the Pandava army.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Time, whose acts are wonderful assembled them on that spot and having made the Kauravas the cause, destroyed them all.
lines.tts_text: Time, whose acts are wonderful assembled them on that spot and having made the Kauravas the cause, destroyed them all.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Bhishma acquainted with choice of weapons, fought for ten days.
lines.tts_text: Bhishma acquainted with choice of weapons, fought for ten days.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Drona protected the Kaurava Vahinis for five days.
lines.tts_text: Drona protected the Kaurava Vahinis for five days.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Kama the desolator of hostile armies fought for two days; and Salya for half a day.
lines.tts_text: Karna the desolator of hostile armies fought for two days; and Salya for half a day.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: After that lasted for half a day the encounter with clubs between Duryodhana and Bhima.
lines.tts_text: After that lasted for half a day the encounter with clubs between Duryodhana and Bheema.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: At the close of that day, Aswatthaman and Kripa destroyed the army of Yudishthira in the night while sleeping without suspicion of danger.
lines.tts_text: At the close of that day, Aswatthaman and Kripaa destroyed the army of Yudhishthira in the night while sleeping without suspicion of danger.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: 'O Saunaka, this best of narrations called Bharata which has begun to be repeated at thy sacrifice, was formerly repeated at the sacrifice of Janamejaya by an intelligent disciple of Vyasa.
lines.tts_text: 'O Shownuhkuh, this best of narrations called Bharata which has begun to be repeated at thy sacrifice, was formerly repeated at the sacrifice of Janamejaya by an intelligent disciple of Vyasa.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: It is divided into several sections; in the beginning are Paushya, Pauloma, and Astika parvas, describing in full the valour and renown of kings.
lines.tts_text: It is divided into several sections; in the beginning are Paushya, Pauloma, and Astika parvas, describing in full the valour and renown of kings.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: It is a work whose description, diction, and sense are varied and wonderful.
lines.tts_text: It is a work whose description, diction, and sense are varied and wonderful.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: It contains an account of various manners and rites.
lines.tts_text: It contains an account of various manners and rites.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: It is accepted by the wise, as the state called Vairagya is by men desirous of final release.
lines.tts_text: It is accepted by the wise, as the state called Vairagya is by men desirous of final release.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: As Self among things to be known, as life among things that are dear, so is this history that furnisheth the means of arriving at the knowledge of Brahma the first among all the sastras.
lines.tts_text: As Self among things to be known, as life among things that are dear, so is this history that furnisheth the means of arriving at the knowledge of Brahma the first among all the Sastras.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: There is not a story current in this world but doth depend upon this history even as the body upon the foot that it taketh.
lines.tts_text: There is not a story current in this world but doth depend upon this history even as the body upon the foot that it taketh.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: As masters of good lineage are ever attended upon by servants desirous of preferment so is the Bharata cherished by all poets.
lines.tts_text: As masters of good lineage are ever attended upon by servants desirous of preferment so is the Bharata cherished by all poets.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: As the words constituting the several branches of knowledge appertaining to the world and the Veda display only vowels and consonants, so this excellent history displayeth only the highest wisdom.
lines.tts_text: As the words constituting the several branches of knowledge appertaining to the world and the Veda display only vowels and consonants, so this excellent history displayeth only the highest wisdom.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: 'Listen, O ye ascetics, to the outlines of the several divisions (parvas) of this history called Bharata, endued with great wisdom, of sections and feet that are wonderful and various, of subtile meanings and logical connections, and embellished with the substance of the Vedas.
lines.tts_text: 'Listen, O ye ascetics, to the outlines of the several divisions of this history called Bharata, endued with great wisdom, of sections and feet that are wonderful and various, of subtile meanings and logical connections, and embellished with the substance of the Vedas.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: 'The first parva is called Anukramanika; the second, Sangraha; then Paushya; then Pauloma; the Astika; then Adivansavatarana.
lines.tts_text: 'The first parva is called Anukramanika; the second, Sangraha; then Paushya; then Pauloma; the Astika; then Adivansavatarana.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then comes the Sambhava of wonderful and thrilling incidents.
lines.tts_text: Then comes the Sambhava of wonderful and thrilling incidents.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then comes Jatugrihadaha (setting fire to the house of lac) and then Hidimbabadha (the killing of Hidimba) parvas; then comes Baka-badha (slaughter of Baka) and then Chitraratha.
lines.tts_text: Then comes Jatugrihadaha and then Hidimbabadha parvas; then comes Baka-badha and then Chitraratha.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The next is called Swayamvara (selection of husband by Panchali), in which Arjuna by the exercise of Kshatriya virtues, won Draupadi for wife.
lines.tts_text: The next is called Svayamvara, in which Arjoona by the exercise of Kshatriya virtues, won Drowpadee for wife.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then comes Vaivahika (marriage).
lines.tts_text: Then comes Vaivahika.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then comes Viduragamana (advent of Vidura), Rajyalabha (acquirement of kingdom), Arjuna-banavasa (exile of Arjuna) and Subhadra-harana (the carrying away of Subhadra).
lines.tts_text: Then comes Viduragamana, Rajyalabha, Arjoona-banavasa and Subhadra-harana.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: After these come Harana-harika, Khandava-daha (the burning of the Khandava forest) and Maya-darsana (meeting with Maya the Asura architect).
lines.tts_text: After these come Harana-harika, Khandava-daha and Maya-darsana.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then come Sabha, Mantra, Jarasandha, Digvijaya (general campaign).
lines.tts_text: Then come Sabha, Mantra, Jarasandha, Digvijaya.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: After Digvijaya come Raja-suyaka, Arghyaviharana (the robbing of the Arghya) and Sisupala-badha (the killing of Sisupala).
lines.tts_text: After Digvijaya come Raja-suyaka, Arghyaviharana and Sisupala-badha.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: After these, Dyuta (gambling), Anudyuta (subsequent to gambling), Aranyaka, and Krimira-badha (destruction of Krimira).
lines.tts_text: After these, Dyuta, Anudyuta, Aranyaka, and Kirmira-badha.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The Arjuna-vigamana (the travels of Arjuna), Kairati.
lines.tts_text: The Arjoona-vigamana, Kairati.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: In the last hath been described the battle between Arjuna and Mahadeva in the guise of a hunter.
lines.tts_text: In the last hath been described the battle between Arjoona and Mahadeva in the guise of a hunter.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: After this Indra-lokavigamana (the journey to the regions of Indra); then that mine of religion and virtue, the highly pathetic Nalopakhyana (the story of Nala).
lines.tts_text: After this Indra-lokavigamana; then that mine of religion and virtue, the highly pathetic Nalopakhyana.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: After this last, Tirtha-yatra or the pilgrimage of the wise prince of the Kurus, the death of Jatasura, and the battle of the Yakshas.
lines.tts_text: After this last, Tirtha-yatra or the pilgrimage of the wise prince of the Kurus, the death of Jatasura, and the battle of the Yakshas.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then the battle with the Nivata-kavachas, Ajagara, and Markandeya-Samasya (meeting with Markandeya).
lines.tts_text: Then the battle with the Nivata-kavachas, Ajagara, and Markandeya-Samasya.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then the meeting of Draupadi and Satyabhama, Ghoshayatra, Mirga-Swapna (dream of the deer).
lines.tts_text: Then the meeting of Drowpadee and Satyabhama, Ghoshayatra, Mriga-Swapna.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then the story of Brihadaranyaka and then Aindradrumna.
lines.tts_text: Then the story of Brihadaranyaka and then Aindradyumna.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then Draupadi-harana (the abduction of Draupadi), Jayadratha-bimoksana (the release of Jayadratha).
lines.tts_text: Then Drowpadee-harana, Jayadratha-bimoksana.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then the story of 'Savitri' illustrating the great merit of connubial chastity.
lines.tts_text: Then the story of 'Savitri' illustrating the great merit of connubial chastity.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: After this last, the story of 'Rama'.
lines.tts_text: After this last, the story of 'Rama'.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The parva that comes next is called 'Kundala-harana' (the theft of the ear-rings).
lines.tts_text: The parva that comes next is called 'Kundala-harana'.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: That which comes next is 'Aranya' and then 'Vairata'.
lines.tts_text: That which comes next is 'Aranya' and then 'Vairata'.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then the entry of the Pandavas and the fulfilment of their promise (of living unknown for one year).
lines.tts_text: Then the entry of the Pandavas and the fulfilment of their promise.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then the destruction of the 'Kichakas', then the attempt to take the kine (of Virata by the Kauravas).
lines.tts_text: Then the destruction of the 'Kichakas', then the attempt to take the kine.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The next is called the marriage of Abhimanyu with the daughter of Virata.
lines.tts_text: The next is called the marriage of Abhimunyu with the daughter of Virata.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The next you must know is the most wonderful parva called Udyoga.
lines.tts_text: The next you must know is the most wonderful parva called Udyoga.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The next must be known by the name of 'Sanjaya-yana' (the arrival of Sanjaya).
lines.tts_text: The next must be known by the name of 'Sanjaya-yana'.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then comes 'Prajagara' (the sleeplessness of Dhritarashtra owing to his anxiety).
lines.tts_text: Then comes 'Prajagara'.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then Sanatsujata, in which are the mysteries of spiritual philosophy.
lines.tts_text: Then Sanatsujata, in which are the mysteries of spiritual philosophy.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then 'Yanasaddhi', and then the arrival of Krishna.
lines.tts_text: Then 'Yanasandhi', and then the arrival of Krishna.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then the story of 'Matali' and then of 'Galava'.
lines.tts_text: Then the story of 'Matali' and then of 'Galava'.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then the stories of 'Savitri', 'Vamadeva', and 'Vainya'.
lines.tts_text: Then the stories of 'Savitri', 'Vamadeva', and 'Vainya'.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then the story of 'Jamadagnya and Shodasarajika'.
lines.tts_text: Then the story of 'Jamadagnya and Shodasarajika'.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then the arrival of Krishna at the court, and then Bidulaputrasasana.
lines.tts_text: Then the arrival of Krishna at the court, and then Vidulaputrasasana.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then the muster of troops and the story of Sheta.
lines.tts_text: Then the muster of troops and the story of Shwayta.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then, must you know, comes the quarrel of the high-souled Karna.
lines.tts_text: Then, must you know, comes the quarrel of the high-souled Karna.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then the march to the field of the troops of both sides.
lines.tts_text: Then the march to the field of the troops of both sides.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The next hath been called numbering the Rathis and Atirathas.
lines.tts_text: The next hath been called numbering the Rathis and Atirathas.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then comes the arrival of the messenger Uluka which kindled the wrath (of the Pandavas).
lines.tts_text: Then comes the arrival of the messenger Uluka which kindled the wrath.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The next that comes, you must know, is the story of Amba.
lines.tts_text: The next that comes, you must know, is the story of Amba.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then comes the thrilling story of the installation of Bhishma as commander-in-chief.
lines.tts_text: Then comes the thrilling story of the installation of Bhishma as commander-in-chief.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The next is called the creation of the insular region Jambu; then Bhumi; then the account about the formation of islands.
lines.tts_text: The next is called the creation of the insular region Jambu; then Bhumi; then the account about the formation of islands.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then comes the 'Bhagavat-gita'; and then the death of Bhishma.
lines.tts_text: Then comes the 'Bhagavat-gita'; and then the death of Bhishma.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then the installation of Drona; then the destruction of the 'Sansaptakas'.
lines.tts_text: Then the installation of Drona; then the destruction of the 'Sansaptakas'.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then the death of Abhimanyu; and then the vow of Arjuna (to slay Jayadratha).
lines.tts_text: Then the death of Abhimunyu; and then the vow of Arjoona.
lines.direction: a sacred vow before assembled kings

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then the death of Jayadratha, and then of Ghatotkacha.
lines.tts_text: Then the death of Jayadratha, and then of Ghatotkacha.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then, must you know, comes the story of the death of Drona of surprising interest.
lines.tts_text: Then, must you know, comes the story of the death of Drona of surprising interest.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The next that comes is called the discharge of the weapon called Narayana.
lines.tts_text: The next that comes is called the discharge of the weapon called Naaraayana.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then, you know, is Karna, and then Salya.
lines.tts_text: Then, you know, is Karna, and then Salya.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then comes the immersion in the lake, and then the encounter (between Bhima and Duryodhana) with clubs.
lines.tts_text: Then comes the immersion in the lake, and then the encounter with clubs.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then comes Saraswata, and then the descriptions of holy shrines, and then genealogies.
lines.tts_text: Then comes Saraswata, and then the descriptions of holy shrines, and then genealogies.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then comes Sauptika describing incidents disgraceful (to the honour of the Kurus).
lines.tts_text: Then comes Sauptika describing incidents disgraceful.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then comes the 'Aisika' of harrowing incidents.
lines.tts_text: Then comes the 'Aishika' of harrowing incidents.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then comes 'Jalapradana' oblations of water to the manes of the deceased, and then the wailings of the women.
lines.tts_text: Then comes 'Jalapradaana' oblations of water to the manes of the deceased, and then the wailings of the women.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The next must be known as 'Sraddha' describing the funeral rites performed for the slain Kauravas.
lines.tts_text: The next must be known as 'Sraddha' describing the funeral rites performed for the slain Kauravas.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then comes the destruction of the Rakshasa Charvaka who had assumed the disguise of a Brahmana (for deceiving Yudhishthira).
lines.tts_text: Then comes the destruction of the Rakshasa Charvaka who had assumed the disguise of a Brahmana.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then the coronation of the wise Yudhishthira.
lines.tts_text: Then the coronation of the wise Yudhishthira.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The next is called the 'Grihapravibhaga'.
lines.tts_text: The next is called the 'Grihapravibhaga'.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then comes 'Santi', then 'Rajadharmanusasana', then 'Apaddharma', then 'Mokshadharma'.
lines.tts_text: Then comes 'Santi', then 'Rajadharmanusasana', then 'Apaddharma', then 'Mokshadharma'.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Those that follow are called respectively 'Suka-prasna-abhigamana', 'Brahma-prasnanusana', the origin of 'Durvasa', the disputations with Maya.
lines.tts_text: Those that follow are called respectively 'Suka-prasna-abhigamana', 'Brahma-prasnanusana', the origin of 'Durvasa', the disputations with Maya.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The next is to be known as 'Anusasanika'.
lines.tts_text: The next is to be known as 'Anusasanika'.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then the ascension of Bhishma to heaven.
lines.tts_text: Then the ascension of Bhishma to heaven.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then the horse-sacrifice, which when read purgeth all sins away.
lines.tts_text: Then the horse-sacrifice, which when read purgeth all sins away.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The next must be known as the 'Anugita' in which are words of spiritual philosophy.
lines.tts_text: The next must be known as the 'Anugita' in which are words of spiritual philosophy.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Those that follow are called 'Asramvasa', 'Puttradarshana' (meeting with the spirits of the deceased sons), and the arrival of Narada.
lines.tts_text: Those that follow are called 'Asramvasa', 'Puttradarshana', and the arrival of Naaruda.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The next is called 'Mausala' which abounds with terrible and cruel incidents.
lines.tts_text: The next is called 'Mausala' which abounds with terrible and cruel incidents.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then comes 'Mahaprasthanika' and ascension to heaven.
lines.tts_text: Then comes 'Mahaprasthanika' and ascension to heaven.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then comes the Purana which is called Khilvansa.
lines.tts_text: Then comes the Purana which is called Khilvansa.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: In this last are contained 'Vishnuparva', Vishnu's frolics and feats as a child, the destruction of 'Kansa', and lastly, the very wonderful 'Bhavishyaparva' (in which there are prophecies regarding the future).
lines.tts_text: In this last are contained 'Vishnuparva', Vishnu's frolics and feats as a child, the destruction of 'Kansa', and lastly, the very wonderful 'Bhavishyaparva'.
